title: Additivity of the Frobenius traces along an open–closed decomposition
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, let $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$
be a closed immersion with complementary open immersion
$j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$,
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be their base changes to $k$. Let
$(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a strict Weil complex
of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex].

1. For $h\in\{i,j\}$ with source $W\in\{Z,U\}$, one has
$h\,g_W=g_X\,h$, and the composite
$$
h^*\varphi:\;
Lg_W^*Lh^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lh^*Lg_X^*K
\xrightarrow{\ Lh^*\varphi\ }Lh^*K
$$
of the canonical pullback identification with $Lh^*\varphi$ makes
$(Lh^*K,h^*\varphi)$ a strict Weil complex on $W$; its iterates of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map] are
$(h^*\varphi)^{[m]}=Lh^*\varphi^{[m]}\circ c_{h,m}$, with
$c_{h,m}:Lg_W^{m*}Lh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lg_X^{m*}$ the canonical
identification.
1. For every $m\geq1$, with $F_{c,-}^{\,m}$ the global geometric
Frobenius operators of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] for these
Weil structures,
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,j^*K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(U,j^*K)\bigr)
+
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,i^*K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*K)\bigr)
$$
in $A$. These are categorical traces of perfect complexes in the
sense of [def-trf-categorical-trace]; no trace of an individual
cohomology module occurs.
1. *(Frobenius coefficient morphisms.)* Let instead
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ carry an arbitrary Frobenius coefficient
morphism $\psi:L\Phi_X^*K\to K$ of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], with no Weil structure and no
invertibility. For $h\in\{i,j\}$ with source $W$ one has
$h\,\Phi_W=\Phi_X\,h$, the composite
$h^*\psi:L\Phi_W^*Lh^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*L\Phi_X^*K
\xrightarrow{Lh^*\psi}Lh^*K$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism on
$W$ with iterates $(h^*\psi)_m=Lh^*\psi_m\circ c'_{h,m}$, where
$c'_{h,m}:L\Phi_W^{m*}Lh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*L\Phi_X^{m*}$ is the
canonical identification, and for every $m\geq1$ the global operators
$F_{c,m}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] satisfy
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(j^*\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(U,j^*K)\bigr)
+
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(i^*\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*K)\bigr).
$$

The proof below uses the Weil maps only as morphisms: the
invertibility of $\varphi$ is used only to stay inside the category
$D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}$ on which $F_{c,-}^{\,m}$ is defined.

proof.text:
Restricted structures and iterates. Since $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, the equalities $hg_W=g_Xh$ for $h=i,j$ are equalities of maps of fibre products. The open squares for all powers are Cartesian by [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square]; the closed Galois square is also Cartesian: base change of the subscheme $Z_0\times_{k_0}k$ by the coefficient-field automorphism gives this same subscheme, with its same defining ideal. The finite-type scheme $X$ has a finite affine cover by finitely generated $k$-algebras. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-noetherian-spectrum] these affine spaces are Noetherian topologically, since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a singleton. Restricting an ascending chain of opens to each of the finitely many affine opens shows that it stabilizes on $X$. Thus every open of $X$, in particular $U$, is quasi-compact: any open cover admits a maximal finite union by the ascending-chain condition, and maximality forces that union to be the covered open. Thus the open immersion $j$ is finite type (it is locally the identity and is quasi-compact); the closed immersion $i$ is finite type, locally being given by a ring quotient. Both are separated. By [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i), $Lh^*K\in D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$. The displayed map $h^*\varphi$ is a composite of isomorphisms, hence gives the strict Weil structure of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex]. Under the pullback-composition identifications [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], the product defining $(h^*\varphi)^{[m]}$ in [def-trf-iterated-weil-map] is
$Lh^*(\varphi\circ Lg_X^*\varphi\circ\cdots\circ Lg_X^{(m-1)*}\varphi)\circ c_{h,m}$.
Indeed the case $m=1$ is its definition; multiplying by the next pulled-back factor replaces $c_{h,m}$ by $c_{h,m+1}$. This identity of comparisons is checked termwise on inverse-image sheaves, where both bracketings identify the inverse image along the same composite map, and descends to complexes. This proves clause 1. The same multiplication, using the recursion of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], proves the iterate formula for $h^*\psi$, since naturality of the $q$-power scheme Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] gives $h\Phi_W=\Phi_Xh$.

Construct the localization filtration before taking derived compact cohomology. Write $S_X(C)$ for the filtered complex with $F^0C=C$, $F^1C=j_!j^*C$, $F^2C=0$. The open is quasi-compact by Step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], with constant ring sheaf $A_X$, in each degree: the counit and unit form a short exact sequence of complexes
$0\to j_!j^*C\to C\to i_*i^*C\to0$.
Thus $\omega S_X(C)=C$, $\operatorname{gr}^1S_X(C)=j_!j^*C$, and $\operatorname{gr}^0S_X(C)=i_*i^*C$. The constant-coefficient inverse images are exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and the cited localization lemma gives exactness of $j_!$ and $i_*$. Since these functors are exact, $S_X$ takes a quasi-isomorphism to a filtered quasi-isomorphism, so it descends to a functor on the ordinary derived category. Its underlying triangle is the specified localization triangle [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]. This is the explicit filtered section, not a triangulated category of strict Weil pairs.

Fix $t=g_X^m$ and $u=\varphi^{[m]}:Lt^*K\to K$. The open exchange [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] identifies the filtration on $Lt^*S_X(K)$ with that on $S_X(Lt^*K)$: on the total complex it is the identity, and on $F^1$ it is $b_t:Lt^*j_!j^*K\simeq j_!Lt_U^*j^*K$. Compatibility with the inclusions is the counit identity: restriction to $U$ makes both maps the identity, and $j_!\dashv j^*$ identifies their Hom sets. Therefore $S_X(u)$ gives an actual filtered morphism
$\widetilde u:Lt^*S_X(K)\to S_X(K)$.
Its total map is $u$ and its degree-1 graded map is $j_!(h^*\varphi)^{[m]}\circ b_t$ for $h=j$. Its degree-0 graded map is the map induced on the quotient, namely $i_*(i^*\varphi)^{[m]}\circ e_t$ with $e_t:Lt^*i_*\to i_*Lt_Z^*$ the adjunction mate. To see the last identification, transpose it under $i^*\dashv i_*$; the closed counit is invertible by [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], and both transposes are $i^*u$ after $i^*Lt^*\simeq Lt_Z^*i^*$. Thus it is the specified closed component, not merely a choice of third triangle map.

source.place: Step 2; filtered section: Varshavsky §5.2.3; pro-etale exact sequence: Stacks Tags 09BM, 09AH

proof.text:
Apply filtered compact cohomology. The two sheaf-localization pieces are in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](iii),(iv) applied to $i,j$ and the restrictions of Step 1. Thus all compact-support comparisons below remain on their stated finite-Tor constructible domains. By [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts], $R\Gamma_c(X,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_sRa_{X!}$ has a filtered lift: use a compactification $a_X=pj$, which exists by [thm-nagata-compactification] since $a_X$ is separated finite type and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, hence qcqs, to form $R^Fp_*j_!^F$ and then the exact point fibre functor of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], with compact cohomology as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. The compact base-change map along $g_X^m$ over $g_s^m$ has a filtered lift $\widetilde\beta_t$ as well, because it is the canonical exchange built from the sheaf-derived adjunction maps. On the point fibre the constant-coefficient identification removes the pullback by $g_s^m$. Consequently
$\widetilde E=R\Gamma_c^F(X,\widetilde u)\circ\widetilde\beta_t$
is an endomorphism of $R\Gamma_c^F(X,S_X(K))$ in $DF^+(A)$. Forgetting the filtration gives
$E_K=R\Gamma_c(X,u)\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}=F_{c,K}^{\,m}$
by [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description]. Associated graded gives the same composite on the two pieces, with the two graded coefficient maps found in Step 2; this follows from the associated-graded compatibility of both functors and transformations in the filtered-lift lemma. This constructs the filtered origin required for trace additivity. It does not infer that origin from the existence of a commuting triple in the ordinary derived category.

Identify the two graded operators. For $h=j,i$, let $\lambda_h:R\Gamma_c(X,Rh_!N)\simeq R\Gamma_c(W,N)$ be the composition isomorphism of [prop-functor-package](3); For $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] gives finiteness and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] gives properness, so that clause identifies $Ri_!=Ri_*$. Write $b_{t,h}:Lt^*Rh_!\to Rh_!Lt_W^*$ for the open exchange, respectively the closed quotient mate of Step 2. Under $\lambda_h$ the exchange for $a_X$ followed by $R\Gamma_c(X,b_{t,h})$ is the exchange for $a_W=a_Xh$. More explicitly, suppressing the canonical point pullback, the equation needed is
$$
\lambda_{h,Lt_W^*N}\,R\Gamma_c(X,b_{t,h})\,\beta_{t,Rh_!N}
=\beta_{t_W,N}\,\lambda_{h,N}.
$$
This is the compact-support vertical-pasting equation of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts], for the square for $h$ above the square for $a_X$, with the composition comparisons $R(a_Xh)_!\simeq Ra_{X!}Rh_!$ inserted. It is computed in compactifications: on the proper direct-image factors use [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3), and on the open factors use the pasting property of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange]. The two pasted pullback squares identify the same composite inverse image. This does not regard $Ra_{X!}$ as a right adjoint to $La_X^*$; the adjunction-mate calculation is on the proper factors only. For the open square, $b_{t,j}$ is the open extension comparison; for the closed square, it is the transpose identified in Step 2. All the compactification-relative exchanges and composition comparisons in this calculation are the canonical ones covered by [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts]. This argument uses arbitrary scheme inverse-image squares and thus also applies to the semilinear Galois maps; it does not apply a theorem requiring $k$-morphisms to them. Naturality in $N$ and the restricted-iterate formula of Step 1 now show that the degree-1 and degree-0 maps of $\widetilde E$ are conjugate through $\lambda_j,\lambda_i$ to $F_{c,j^*K}^{\,m}$ and $F_{c,i^*K}^{\,m}$, by [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description].

Take traces. By [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness], the total compact complex and the two complexes on $U,Z$ have bounded finite cohomology. To verify perfectness without confusing the two uses of $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$, apply [thm-sf-ctf-stability](iv) to the three structure maps: each $Ra_{W!}Lh^*K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$ (and similarly for $W=X$). By [fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect], its derived stalk at $\operatorname{id}_s$ is a bounded finite free $A$-complex. That stalk is the exact point evaluation defining $R\Gamma_c$ in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], so all three compact complexes are perfect in the sense of [def-trf-categorical-trace]. The pullback finite-Tor and constructibility hypotheses were checked in Step 1, and all three structure maps are separated finite type. Hence the two-graded-piece object of Step 3 is in the bounded filtered category with perfect total and graded pieces, and its underlying localization triangle satisfies exactly the filtered-origin hypothesis of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws](2). That law gives $\operatorname{tr}_A(E_K)=\operatorname{tr}_A(\operatorname{gr}^1\widetilde E)+\operatorname{tr}_A(\operatorname{gr}^0\widetilde E)$. Conjugacy invariance, item (1) of the same node, and Step 4 give the identity in clause 2. Every trace is taken on the whole perfect complex.

Noninvertible Frobenius coefficient morphisms. Take instead $t=\Phi_X^m$ and $u=\psi_m$. Step 1 already proves the restriction and iterate assertions; the open square is Cartesian by [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square]. Thus Step 2 constructs the filtered morphism $Lt^*S_X(K)\to S_X(K)$ without inverting $u$. The closed square need not be Cartesian. Let $e:L\Phi_X^{m*}Ri_*\to Ri_*L\Phi_Z^{m*}$ be the ordinary mate for this commutative square, as in [def-exchange-projection]. Its adjoint under $i^*\dashv Ri_*$ is the canonical identification $c'_{i,m}$. For $T_0\in\{X_0,Z_0\}$ and $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, the absolute $q$-power Frobenius of $T$ is $F_T^{(q)}=g_{\sigma}\circ\Phi_T$ with $g_\sigma$ the arithmetic Galois automorphism of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]: on $A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ one has $a\otimes b\mapsto a\otimes b^q\mapsto a^q\otimes b^q$, i.e. $(F_T^{(q)})^\sharp=\Phi_T^\sharp\circ(1\otimes\sigma)$, and both sides are morphisms of schemes agreeing on an affine cover. By [lem-pur-absolute-frobenius-universal-homeomorphism] $F_T^{(q)}$ is a universal homeomorphism, hence so is $\Phi_T=g_\sigma^{-1}F_T^{(q)}$ and so is every iterate $\Phi_T^m$ (composites of universal homeomorphisms). By [lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance], $\Phi_X^{m,-1}\dashv\Phi^m_{X*}$ and $\Phi_Z^{m,-1}\dashv\Phi^m_{Z*}$ are adjoint equivalences; these functors are exact on module sheaves, so they compute the derived functors. Hence $e$, the mate of the identity $\Phi^m_{X*}i_*=i_*\Phi^m_{Z*}$, is the composite of isomorphisms $\Phi_X^{m,-1}i_*\cong\Phi_X^{m,-1}i_*\Phi^m_{Z*}\Phi_Z^{m,-1}=\Phi_X^{m,-1}\Phi^m_{X*}i_*\Phi_Z^{m,-1}\cong i_*\Phi_Z^{m,-1}$, so $e$ is an isomorphism. Hence the pulled-back quotient is identified with $i_*L\Phi_Z^{m*}i^*K$, and its coefficient map is the closed adjunction mate. No geometric-stalk criterion or Cartesian closed square is used.

By [lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial], $\Phi_X$ is finite. Induction on $m$, with [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] at the induction step, gives finiteness of $t=\Phi_X^m$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] therefore makes $t$ proper. Thus [prop-functor-package](3) gives $Rt_*=Rt_!$ and $a_Xt=a_X$. Define
$\beta_t:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\to R\Gamma_c(X,Lt^*K)$
by the unit $K\to Rt_*Lt^*K$, the proper comparison and compact-support composition. Its filtered lift exists by [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts]. By [prop-trf-graph-operator], forgetting the endomorphism $R\Gamma_c^F(X,\widetilde u)\circ\widetilde\beta_t$ gives exactly $F_{c,m}(\psi)$. Its graded maps are the same units with the restricted coefficient morphisms: for $h=j,i$ the equation of Step 4 follows from the composite unit $R_1\eta_2L_1\circ\eta_1$ and mate-pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2), applied to $th=ht_W$, followed by compact-support composition. Hence the graded operators are conjugate to $F_{c,m}(j^*\psi)$ and $F_{c,m}(i^*\psi)$ using [prop-trf-graph-operator] on $U,Z$. Apply the perfectness and filtered trace laws of Step 5. This proves clause 3 without any invertibility assumption on $\psi$.

split_report.summary: Repaired the earlier copy: explicitly construct the sheaf-level localization filtration and use one new generic filtered-operation lifting lemma, rather than infer filtered origin from a triangle morphism. Use general adjunction mates for semilinear Galois maps, and obtain the closed Frobenius comparison from the quotient instead of uncited stalk assertions. No statement change.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1–6 realize the six correspondingly numbered steps of the blueprint proposition and the single filtered-origin/graded-trace step of sk-i-global-additivity; the unit route is unchanged.

tool_uses.why: General adjunction mate pasting and composite-unit formulas identify the graded operators; no node of the unit states this generic categorical calculation.
Supplies the canonical pullback comparisons for restrictions and iterates on the pro-etale sites.
Generic sheaf-level exact localization, needed to construct the filtration rather than infer it from a distinguished triangle.
Generic algebraic-geometric tool ensuring the complementary open is quasi-compact; apply to a finite affine cover over the field.
Specifies the exact point evaluation functor used after the filtered compact-support direct image.

Generic pointwise finite-Tor perfectness criterion: apply at the geometric point of Spec k after compact-support stability, avoiding the ambiguous notation for finite-cohomology versus perfect complexes.
Generic geometric fact that the open square is Cartesian for scheme and Galois Frobenius, used for restrictions in this unit without replacing its filtered trace route.
Generic extension-by-zero base change and its pasting law, required to identify the localization subcomplex under pullback.
The compact-support finiteness input explicitly required by the unit; read only as bounded finite cohomology, with perfectness checked separately by finite-Tor stability and the point criterion.
Generic geometric properness input for the closed immersion, via its finiteness.
Generic fact that finite maps are proper, checked before applying the proper !/* comparison to the closed immersion and scheme Frobenius.
Generic composition lemma used inductively to verify properness of every Frobenius iterate.
Existence of the compactification used to implement filtered compact cohomology; the structure morphism is separated finite type over the affine field spectrum.
The scheme-Frobenius finiteness needed to make every iterate proper is supplied by this generic lemma from the Frobenius unit, not by the construction definition itself.
The canonical closed-square mate used to define the coefficient map in the non-Cartesian Frobenius square.
Pro-etale topos invariance for the universal-homeomorphism Frobenius iterates on X and Z: the adjoint equivalences make the closed-square mate e an isomorphism.

The item statement is unchanged and matches the source. The route is unchanged: a filtered origin, then the filtered trace law prop-trf-trace-formal-laws(2). The proof builds a real filtered object S_X from the pro-étale exact localization sequence, using that U is quasi-compact by lem-sfb-finite-type-noetherian-spectrum. I checked the F^1 identification termwise at sheaf level, and the gr^0 map by transposing along i^*⊣Ri_*. Filtered compact cohomology uses the new lemma with a Nagata compactification. The vertical-pasting equation identifies the graded operators for non-k-linear Galois maps, so fix-lem-exchanges is correctly avoided. Perfectness and conjugacy are correct. The new lemma is true and generic (Stacks 015Q/015S/05U2 filtered derived functors; I checked the adjunction clause and the order of composition in Ex_{!,fe}). It is not a duplicate of lem-trf-filtered-projective-model or of the lem-sp-ce-* nodes, and it does not restate a clause of the item. Small cases checked: U or Z empty, ψ=0, the non-Cartesian closed square for Z=V(t)⊂A^1 under Φ, and Ferrand's Z/4 example. Two repairs, files in fixes/. (1) Step 6 asserted that Φ is surjective on points with no citation. I replaced this with F_T^(q)=g_σ∘Φ_T plus lem-pur-absolute-frobenius-universal-homeomorphism (on route through sk-thm-sf-package), so every Φ^m is a universal homeomorphism, and wrote out the adjoint-equivalence argument that the mate e is an isomorphism. This dropped lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism and added def-trf-scheme-frobenius; proof_deps and tool_uses are updated.
